### English source — DO NOT EDIT

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_BEGIN -->
The Cuban Missile Crisis had a significant impact on the relationship between the United States and Latin America. The crisis highlighted the United States' aggressive foreign policy in the region and strengthened anti-American sentiment. Many Latin American countries saw the United States as a threat to their sovereignty and felt that they could also become targets of U.S. intervention. Additionally, the crisis led to increased tension between the United States and Cuba, which prompted the U.S. to impose a trade embargo on Cuba that remains in place to this day. This further fueled resentment towards the United States in Latin America, as many saw the embargo as an unjust punishment on the Cuban people. Overall, the Cuban Missile Crisis contributed to a strained relationship between the United States and Latin America, which has continued to shape their interactions in the decades since.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_END -->
